summary: Intro discovery with Apex Health Systems focused on Redwood's security posture across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments. Key topics: SOC 2 / ISO 27001, SSO/SAML + SCIM, RBAC, audit logs, encryption/KMS, data residency and retention. Customer leans toward Dedicated or Private due to PHI constraints but wants hosted evaluation for cost comparison. Agreed to send SOC2 artifacts, architecture diagram, and schedule a technical deep dive next week.
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-09-29
Time: 15:00 - 15:42 UTC
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Jordan (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Michael Chen (CISO, Apex), Sofia Alvarez (Head Cloud Ops), David Park (Security Engineer)

[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Jordan Lee, AE at Redwood. With me is Priya, our solutions engineer. How's everyone doing?
[00:08] Michael: Good, thanks. We'll keep this focused - we're evaluating options for LLM inference and need to understand your security posture before we take it to procurement.
[00:15] Priya: Great, that's exactly what we wanted to cover - SOC2, ISO, SSO, RBAC, audit logs, encryption, data residency, retention, the whole set. Happy to go deep where you want.
[00:27] Sofia: High level first - we run PHI workloads, so our preference is Private or Dedicated, but cost is a factor. We need to know what controls are in place for hosted too, because we might prototype there.
[00:40] Jordan: Totally. Quick agenda: compliance artifacts we can share, identity integration (SAML/SCIM), RBAC and least privilege, audit logs and monitoring, encryption/KMS, and data retention/residency. Then capture action items. Sound ok?
[00:50] Michael: Yep. Start with SOC2 and ISO. Do you have a SOC2 Type II? Is Redwood ISO certified?
[00:57] Priya: We have SOC2 Type II - I'll send the most recent report after an NDA, and we also have an ISO 27001 summary; full certificates are available for enterprise contracts. Note: sometimes the transcription says SOC two or ISO twenty seven thousand, sorry.
[01:12] Michael: Cool. Are you audited annually? Pen tests?
[01:16] Priya: Yes, annual SOC2 audits. We do internal pen testing and use third-party pen testers annually; we share pen test summaries for customers on enterprise plans. We also maintain a vulnerability management program and SCA where applicable.
[01:30] David: For Private deployments, who manages the keys? If we go VPC/private, can we bring our own KMS/HSM?
[01:36] Priya: Good question. For Redwood Private, customers can use their own KMS via integrations (Cloud KMS, HSM) - bring-your-own-key (BYOK) is supported. For Hosted, we encrypt at rest and in transit with provider-managed KMS but we offer customer-managed keys on enterprise plans. We'll include KMS integration notes.
[01:52] Sofia: When you say encryption at rest in hosted, is that with provider CMKs or do you rotate keys?
[01:58] Priya: For hosted by default we use provider CMKs with regular rotation; for enterprise customers we can rotate per-customer keys and support external rotation schedules via BYOK.
[02:08] Jordan: Quick interjection - from a compliance perspective, we can provide audit logs and access records for API tokens, model calls, and admin actions. How granular do you need the logs?
[02:18] Michael: We need admin actions, who accessed what data, and exportable logs for retention into our SIEM. Full request-level logs for a 90-day window to start, with options for longer retention.
[02:28] Priya: Redwood exposes audit logs via structured logs and can stream to customer S3 or a logging endpoint, and we have integrations for SIEM (splunk, datadog). For Private/Dedicated, logs can stay in-customer-network and you control retention policies.
[02:43] David: Are there event IDs and user mapping between SSO identities and API tokens? We need traceability from our IdP to actions in the system.
[02:50] Priya: Yes - we map SAML identities to user principals, and we persist token-to-user mapping in logs. We also support SCIM for provisioning, so you can sync groups and users for RBAC.
[03:02] Sofia: SCIM - does it work for our Okta setup? We've had issues with SCIM claims before.
[03:07] Priya: We commonly integrate with Okta, Azure AD, and Google Workspace. We'll share the SAML metadata and a SCIM example for Okta. Typical fields are username, email, groups; we can adapt to your claim mappings.
[03:20] Michael: On RBAC, do you support fine-grained roles? We need to ensure least privilege - for example, policy that devops can spin up test models but cannot access PHI pipelines, while a separate team can run inference on de-identified corpora.
[03:34] Priya: We support role-based permissions at route and model level - built-in roles and custom roles. You can scope access by model, by environment (prod vs dev), and by route. For Dedicated/Private customers we can add additional constraints and integrate with your central identity and SSO.
[03:48] Jordan: Also note you can pin model versions and create rollout policies for safer rollouts - that's operational but relevant for security governance.
[03:55] Michael: About data residency: our PHI must not leave the region. How do Dedicated and Private differ?
[04:02] Priya: Private keeps everything in your VPC or on-prem - control plane can be customer-managed depending on the engagement. Dedicated is reserved capacity in a provider region; you can choose region and we can guarantee the compute and storage remain in that region. Hosted routes may cross regions unless you subscribe to region-specific endpoints. We'll provide the region and data residency doc.
[04:20] David: Does Redwood ever cache prompts or KV cache that might persist PHI? We need to ensure no sensitive data is cached without masking.
[04:27] Priya: We have KV/prefix caching for performance; for PHI customers we can disable caching or restrict it to ephemeral in-memory caches with no persistence. We also support auto redaction hooks and retention policies so caches are not written to disk.
[04:41] Sofia: What about model telemetry and training data usage? We need assurances that hosted model usage isn't used for training external models.
[04:49] Jordan: Redwood's policy is we do not use customer data to train models. For hosted enterprise we have contractual terms that prohibit using customer prompts for model improvement unless explicitly opted-in. We'll surface the contract language too.
[05:00] Michael: Great. On SSO - we need service accounts for automation. How are service accounts represented and audited?
[05:07] Priya: Service accounts are tokenized, you can attach scopes and expiration, and they are tied to an owner and authentication method. They appear in audit logs and can be forced-rotated. We also support short-lived tokens and integration with your secrets manager.
[05:19] David: Secrets manager - do you support HashiCorp Vault or only cloud-native secret stores?
[05:23] Priya: We have integrations with Vault, AWS Secrets Manager, and GCP Secret Manager. For Private we can do direct HSM/Vault connectivity inside your network.
[05:33] Michael: Okay. A few procurement items - liability limits, breach notification timelines, and data processing addendum (DPA). Can you share a sample DPA?
[05:42] Jordan: Yes, we have a standard DPA and can share a redline-friendly version. For breach notifications we have contractual SLAs; we'll include those in the package.
[05:52] Sofia: Any certifications for healthcare specifically? HIPAA?
[05:56] Priya: We operate in health stacks with BAAs - for Private and Dedicated customers we sign BAAs. Hosted requires an enterprise contract and controls to support HIPAA; we'll route that to legal.
[06:08] Michael: Logging retention - default hosted retention is what? And can we push logs to our S3 with lifecycle rules?
[06:14] Priya: Default is 30 days for request-level logs in hosted, but enterprise tiers allow configurable retention. Logs can be exported to your S3 with lifecycle rules or to your SIEM with streaming. For Private, you control retention fully.
[06:27] David: About monitoring and alerting - do you provide IDS/IPS logs or just application logs?
[06:33] Priya: We provide application audit logs, runtime metrics, and can integrate with your security tooling to stream alerts. For Dedicated/Private deployments we can surface host-level telemetry as part of the contract.
[06:46] Jordan: Quick note on model variants and fallbacks - operationally we have policy routing and fallbacks to cheaper model variants; that's more about availability but worth noting because you may want to restrict which models can see PHI.
[06:57] Sofia: Good point. We'll want to limit PHI routes to specific models and enforce canary policies.
[07:03] Priya: You can create route-level policies and model allowlists/denylists. Those are enforced at the gateway.
[07:11] Michael: Any details on penetration test windows and disclosure? We may want to run our own tests against a Private deployment.
[07:18] Priya: For Private, customers can run pen tests inside their environment; we request a standard test plan and coordination to avoid service disruption. For hosted, we have a penetration testing policy and coordinate with customers - we'll share that doc.
[07:30] David: Ok. A question about audit logs schema - do you include request/response bodies or just metadata? We usually avoid storing full payloads with PHI.
[07:38] Priya: By default we log metadata (timestamps, user, route, model, token usage, status codes). Request/response bodies are not persisted in hosted logs unless explicitly enabled - and in enterprise setups we can redact or disable body capture. We'll include the log schema sample.
[07:55] Jordan: Sounds like the big decisions leaning toward Dedicated/Private for PHI, but you'd like to see artifacts to evaluate hosted first?
[08:03] Michael: Exactly. We'll do a quick hosted pilot for cost/latency, but production will likely be Dedicated or Private. Procurement needs SOC2, DPA, BAA, and architecture diagram.
[08:12] Sofia: Also need SSO integration guide and RBAC examples so our identity team can sign off.
[08:18] Priya: We'll put together a package: SOC2 Type II, ISO summary, DPA/BAA template, architecture diagram for Private and Dedicated, SCIM/SAML guide, and the audit log schema. Also KMS integration notes.
[08:29] Michael: Timeline - we need those docs for next Tuesday. Can you get them to us by then?
[08:34] Jordan: Yes - we'll send the docs by Friday COB and follow up with the deep technical session next week.
[08:41] Sofia: Can we schedule the SE deep-dive for Tuesday morning? Our networking lead is only available then.
[08:45] Priya: I can do Tuesday 09:00 PT. I'll send a calendar invite.
[08:51] David: One more technical: how do you handle KV cache eviction and logs for cached items? We want to make sure PHI isn't written to durable storage.
[08:58] Priya: For PHI routes we can disable persistent caching and set TTLs to zero so data remains in ephemeral memory. We'll share the cache config doc and default eviction policy.
[09:10] Jordan: Anything else?
[09:12] Michael: One ask - include a short runbook for incident response and what telemetry you can provide during an incident.
[09:18] Priya: We'll include an incident response runbook summary.
[09:22] Jordan: Great. Recap of next steps: send SOC2/ISO/DPA/BAA, architecture diagram, SAML/SCIM guide, audit log schema, KMS notes; schedule SE deep dive Tuesday 09:00 PT; customer to share retention requirements.
[09:38] Michael: Sounds good, thanks.
[09:40] Sofia: Thanks everyone.
[09:42] Jordan: Thanks, we'll follow up.

[END]
